note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

episodes.title: Walking bundle of habits
episodes.hook: Most of what you did today, you didn't decide. Your habits did.
episodes.angle: Most daily actions run on habit, not choice. Example: driving home and not remembering the trip.

episodes.title: Your brain is clay
episodes.hook: Your brain is like paper that remembers every fold.
episodes.angle: Each repetition makes the next one easier, for good or bad habits. Example: folding a letter along the same crease.

episodes.title: Character sets like plaster
episodes.hook: By thirty, your character starts to set like plaster.
episodes.angle: Habits harden over time, so early choices matter more. Example: two friends at 20 and at 35, one who kept the reading habit.

episodes.title: Habits free your mind
episodes.hook: Hating routine? Routine is what lets you think.
episodes.angle: Automating small things frees attention for important ones. Example: the person who lays out clothes and saves morning energy.

episodes.title: Start strong
episodes.hook: Start a new habit with as much force as you can.
episodes.angle: Launch with a strong, public, all-in decision. Example: telling five friends you're running the race and booking the ticket.

episodes.title: Never allow an exception
episodes.hook: 'Just this once' is how every habit dies.
episodes.angle: Each exception undoes many wins, like dropping a ball of yarn. Example: skipping the gym 'just once' on Monday.

episodes.title: Act on it now
episodes.hook: A good intention you don't act on makes you worse, not better.
episodes.angle: Feeling inspired without acting trains you to do nothing. Example: watching motivation videos for an hour instead of working.

episodes.title: The first chance
episodes.hook: Take the very first chance to act on your decision.
episodes.angle: Seize the first opportunity to act on each resolution. Example: deciding to call your dad more and calling him right now.

episodes.title: Do one hard thing daily
episodes.hook: Do one small useless hard thing every day.
episodes.angle: Practising discomfort keeps your will ready for real tests. Example: a cold shower, taking the stairs.

episodes.title: Insurance for your will
episodes.hook: Discipline is insurance you pay for before you need it.
episodes.angle: Daily effort is like a premium paid; when hard times come, you're covered. Example: the person who keeps calm in a crisis because she's done hard things before.

episodes.title: The drunk who doesn't count
episodes.hook: 'This one doesn't count' — but your nerves are counting.
episodes.angle: Every action is recorded by the body, even ones you dismiss. Example: the smoker who says each cigarette is the last one.

episodes.title: Act as if
episodes.hook: Want to feel confident? Act confident first.
episodes.angle: Action shapes feeling, not only the other way around. Example: standing tall before a presentation.

episodes.title: Small daily choices
episodes.hook: You're not ruined by one bad day. You're built by ordinary ones.
episodes.angle: Character is the sum of small daily choices. Example: a student who studies 20 minutes every day versus one who crams.

episodes.title: Wake up on time
episodes.hook: The fight for your life starts with the alarm clock.
episodes.angle: The first decision of the day trains every other. Example: two people, one who gets up at the first alarm.

episodes.title: Nobody is born disciplined
episodes.hook: Disciplined people aren't stronger than you. They just started earlier.
episodes.angle: Discipline is a habit you build, not a talent. Example: the friend who seems 'naturally' disciplined but built it at age 15.
